channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Presidential Election: Digital Signatures and Primaries
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's presidential election process is underway, with 11 candidates, including incumbent Sadyr Japarov. A notable feature is the use of digital technology, specifically the "Tunduk" app, for collecting required signatures. This digital approach presents both opportunities and challenges for candidates and voters.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Achieves Significant Road Construction Milestones in 2026
item.description: A session of the "Ala-Toо" parliamentary group discussed the progress of road construction, irrigation systems, and water supply in Kyrgyzstan. The Deputy Minister of Transport and Communications reported that 1903 kilometers of roads have been asphalted nationwide by 2026, an increase of 735 kilometers compared to the previous year. Future plans aim to construct over 2000 kilometers of roads annually starting from 2027.

item.title: Turkish-Qatari Consortium to Build New Bukhara International Airport
item.description: Uzbekistan Airports announced the completion of a tender for the construction and management of the New Bukhara International Airport. A consortium of Turkey's Limak İnşaat and Qatar's Hamad Bin Khalid Contracting Company won the bid. They will undertake a joint project to build and manage the airport, with a public-private partnership agreement expected soon for 23 years.

item.title: Taliban Prime Minister Meets Russian Deputy Prime Minister to Boost Ties
item.description: Taliban Prime Minister Mullah Mohammad Hassan Akhund held talks with Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexei Overchuk to strengthen bilateral relations and expand economic cooperation. The meeting, also attended by foreign ministers, was described as a significant step. Akhund welcomed Russia's recognition of the Taliban, citing improved security for investment.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Implement Fair Alimony System, Strengthen Child Rights Protections
item.description: Uzbekistan will implement a fair system for determining alimony amounts based on living costs. The country will also strengthen efforts to combat discrimination against women and children's rights. A system will be created to ensure quality education and talent development for children of citizens working abroad in labor migration.

item.title: Kazakhstan Calls for Strengthening UN Water Architecture at COP31
item.description: Kazakhstan urged strengthening the UN's water architecture during a special event at COP31 in Antalya. The delegation presented the country's achievements in water resource management and its regional priorities. Kazakhstan proposed creating an International Water Organization to enhance UN coordination and effectiveness, a proposal supported by international organizations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Holds Meeting on Preventing Domestic Violence and Supporting Victims
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers, Ulan Mamatkanov, chaired a meeting on preventing domestic violence, protecting victims, and providing timely support. Discussions focused on interagency cooperation and the effectiveness of current measures. Directives were issued to strengthen prevention efforts and develop a plan for 2027.

item.title: Kazakh Political Analysts Note Increased Anti-Corruption Investigations Against Top Executives
item.description: Political analysts in Kazakhstan conclude that even top managers of major companies are not immune to investigations, indicating a tough stance against corruption. This reflects the state's commitment to the principle of "Law and Order," a cornerstone of the new constitution, ensuring punishment regardless of position or influence, as stated by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev.

item.title: Turkish-Qatari consortium wins tender to build and operate new airport in Bukhara
item.description: A consortium of Turkey's Limak İnşaat and Qatar's HBK Contracting has won the international tender to build and operate a new international airport in Bukhara under a public-private partnership. The project will be implemented on a Build-Transfer-Operate model. The private partner will construct and manage the passenger terminal and related infrastructure, while the state partner will handle the runway and apron.

item.title: Projects to expand Bukhara refinery production capacity presented to president
item.description: Projects aimed at expanding the production capacity of the Bukhara oil refinery were presented to the president. One project, costing $328 million, will enable the production of Euro-5 compliant AI-92 and AI-95 gasoline, with an expected annual output of 1.1 million tons. This initiative is projected to save up to $150 million annually by reducing imported fuel additives.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Anti-Cancer Drug DVC Faces Market Entry Delay Until Mid-2027
item.description: Kazakhstan's anti-cancer drug DVC is now projected to launch in mid-2027, a delay attributed to stringent clinical trial requirements. The Ministry of Science and Higher Education confirmed the first phase's completion and progression to the second. Development is ongoing, with finalization expected by mid-next year before market release.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Fines for Delayed Housing Handover and 10-Year Guarantees
item.description: A new draft law in Uzbekistan may require developers to pay a 0.01% daily fine for delayed housing handover. The legislation also proposes a minimum 10-year warranty for new homes and mandates that at least 70% of construction be financed through banks, strengthening developer accountability.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Bukhara Refinery to Invest $328 Million in Euro-5 Gasoline Production by 2029
item.description: Uzbekistan's Bukhara Refinery will invest $328 million to launch Euro-5 standard gasoline production by the second quarter of 2029. The upgrade aims to produce 1.1 million tons of Euro-5 fuel annually, create 200 jobs, and save up to $150 million yearly by reducing imported fuel additive purchases.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Minister Visits National Pavilion at COP31 Climate Conference
item.description: Adylbek Kasymaliev, Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan, visited the national pavilion at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey. The pavilion showcases Kyrgyzstan's potential in international climate platforms, export and investment opportunities, and national cultural heritage.

item.title: Astana and Bishkek Suppress Analysts, Losing Touch with Reality
item.description: Authorities in Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan are increasingly suppressing independent analysts, mirroring tactics used against independent media. This includes digital censorship, criminal cases, and personal blackmail. This crackdown, particularly evident in the post-Kantar period in Kazakhstan, risks alienating experts and leading to social unrest.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Urges Citizens to Maintain Unity and Resist Provocations
item.description: Political analyst Bakyt Baketaev stated that President Sadyr Japarov's warning against divisive actions and inciting inter-ethnic hatred was timely. With advanced surveillance technology, authorities can quickly identify lawbreakers. Baketaev stressed the need for vigilance amid global geopolitical tensions to preserve peace and stability.

item.title: Almaty Resident Accuses Clinic of Negligence After Father's Near-Fatal Experience
item.description: An Almaty resident has filed a complaint against EMIRMED clinic, alleging medical negligence led to her father's near-fatal condition. After surgery for rectal pain, his condition worsened, and doctors initially dismissed his symptoms as the flu. He was later diagnosed with sepsis and required emergency surgery.

item.title: New Tashkent Projects to Receive Tax Benefits Under Special Economic Regime
item.description: Uzbekistan has introduced a special legal regime for large urban development projects in New Tashkent and the Shirin massif in Samarkand. Projects valued at over $50 million will benefit from tax exemptions for 20 years, including property and land taxes, and a reduced profit tax rate on real estate rentals and sales.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Security Council to Convene Emergency Meeting on Logistics Sector Corruption
item.description: Kazakhstan's Security Council will hold an emergency meeting chaired by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev to address issues in the transport and logistics sector. The meeting follows the detention of the heads of Samruk-Kazyna and Kazakhstan Temir Zholy on corruption charges. The President will emphasize adherence to the 'Law and Order' principle.

item.title: Kazakh President convenes Security Council amid arrests of state company heads
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has called a Security Council meeting following the detention of the heads of "Samruk-Kazyna" and "Kazakhstan Temir Zholy" (KTZ). The specific reasons for the detentions and the council's agenda were not immediately disclosed.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes trust fund for Lake Issyk-Kul preservation at UN climate conference
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is promoting the initiative to establish a trust fund for the preservation of Lake Issyk-Kul within the framework of the United Nations. Special Representative Dinara Kemelova stated that the melting glaciers and decreasing water levels of the lake are a serious warning. The proposal was discussed at the COP31 conference.

item.title: Kazakh President to Address National Company Leaders' Arrests
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev will hold a Security Council meeting on November 13 to outline the state's position on the detention of leaders from "Samruk-Kazyna" and "Kazakhstan Temir Zholy." The meeting will focus on the transport and logistics sector, emphasizing adherence to the "Law and Order" principle and personal accountability of national company heads.

item.title: Two Women Killed in Faryab Province Amid Rising Insecurity
item.description: Local sources report that two women were killed and two men injured in a shooting incident in Faryab Province. The incident, believed to be a result of domestic violence, occurred in the Damqol area of Maimana. This marks the fifth reported case of women being killed in Afghanistan in the past month.

item.title: Kazakh President convenes Security Council meeting on corruption arrests
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev will convene a Security Council meeting on November 13 to address corruption allegations. The meeting will focus on the transport and logistics sector and the recent detentions of heads of "Samruk-Kazyna" and "Kazakhstan Temir Zholy." The President will outline the state's position on the matter and emphasize accountability.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman strengthen economic ties through upcoming business forum
item.description: Uzbekistan and Oman are expanding cooperation across various sectors, including politics, economy, and tourism. An upcoming business forum in Muscat on November 16-17 aims to boost trade and investment. The event will explore collaboration in trade, investment, transport, logistics, energy, industry, agriculture, and tourism, with an "Made in Uzbekistan" exhibition.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Build Resorts for Pensioners Amid Rising Pensioner Population
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to build resorts for pensioners in Issyk-Kul and Osh regions, according to Baktiyar Aliev, Chairman of the Social Fund. The number of pensioners has doubled to 826,000 since 2010. The average pension has also increased significantly, requiring substantial additional funding.

item.title: Kazakhstan President's Address: Youth, Science, and Agriculture Discussed in Turkistan
item.description: Representatives including a Kurultai deputy and vice-ministers held meetings in Turkistan to discuss priorities from the President's Address to the Nation. Key topics included strengthening social cohesion, increasing youth civic engagement, and promoting national values. The importance of an educated, hardworking, and innovative younger generation was emphasized.

item.title: Kazakhstan Tightens Grip on Experts and Civil Society, Shrinking Civic Space
item.description: Human rights activist Yevgeniy Zhovtis discusses the increasing pressure on experts and civil society in Kazakhstan, leading to a shrinking civic space for academics, political scientists, and rights defenders. He notes that while private dissent is tolerated, public expression of differing opinions is increasingly targeted by the state.

item.title: European Parliament Declares Deportation of Ukrainian Children to Russia as Genocide
item.description: The European Parliament adopted a resolution labeling Russia's actions concerning Ukrainian children as genocide. 536 MEPs voted in favor, with 8 against and 37 abstentions. The resolution stated that the return of children should not be linked to territorial concessions or prisoner exchanges. EU foreign policy chief Josep Borrell condemned the policy, personally approved by Vladimir Putin.

item.title: Almaty Industrial Zone Drives City's Economic Growth and Production
item.description: The Almaty Industrial Zone (IZA) is now the city's main industrial engine, accounting for over 44% of its total industry. In the first nine months of 2026, Almaty enterprises produced 1.97 trillion tenge worth of goods, a 22.2% increase year-on-year, largely due to IZA residents. The zone has generated 3.65 trillion tenge in production and 115.8 billion tenge in taxes.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Expand Forest Cover to 14.7 Million Hectares
item.description: Kazakhstan aims to increase its forest cover to 14.7 million hectares. A roundtable discussion focused on developing forest potential and its role in achieving ecological and climate goals. The event addressed issues like forest fires, illegal logging, and land erosion, emphasizing the need to improve legislation and preserve ecosystems.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Public Sphere Sterilized as Experts Face Online Attacks and Blacklists
item.description: A Kazakhstani political scientist discusses the shrinking of public discourse in Kazakhstan, where experts who voice dissenting opinions are allegedly targeted by bot attacks, spam, and algorithmic manipulation. Officials reportedly silence journalists and bloggers who criticize mid-level bureaucrats, creating an 'artificial reality' devoid of criticism.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan Pledge Joint Efforts to Conserve Endangered Saiga Antelopes
item.description: Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan have agreed to collaborate on protecting the saiga antelope, a vulnerable Central Asian species. A signed memorandum outlines cooperation in conservation, research, and population restoration. Joint monitoring of saiga numbers and migration routes, data exchange, and anti-poaching efforts are key components.

item.title: Almaty Overhauls Water Supply System to Ensure Clean Water for All Residents
item.description: Almaty is undertaking a large-scale modernization of its water management system to guarantee 100% access to clean drinking water, especially in newly developed and remote areas. The city administration is prioritizing the construction of new water sources and the upgrade of existing networks to meet growing demand and climate challenges.

item.title: Kazakhstan Faces Risk of New 'Kantar' Events Amidst Shrinking Free Speech
item.description: Analyst Serik Beisembaev warns that diminishing freedom of speech and increased state control over information in Kazakhstan heighten the risk of repeating the January 2022 'Kantar' events. He argues that attempts to monopolize truth create an information vacuum, breeding rumors and manipulation, reminiscent of Soviet tactics.

item.title: Putin to Discuss Ukraine Conflict Resolution With US Negotiators
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin is expected to meet with US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to discuss ways to resolve the Ukraine conflict. Preliminary talks have occurred, but no agreement has been reached. The meeting aims to review potential solutions.

item.title: 98% of Households in Kyrgyzstan's Issyk-Kul Region Equipped with Smart Electricity Meters
item.description: In Kyrgyzstan's Issyk-Kul region, 98% of household electricity consumers, totaling 121,460 out of 124,429, have been equipped with smart meters. The Issyk-Kul Electric Networks Enterprise reported that remaining meters are being installed in unoccupied homes and remote pastures.

item.title: Riot at Kazakhstan's Aktobe Prison; Inmates Who Cut Wrists Face New Charges
item.description: A riot has occurred at the No. 8 colony in Aktobe, Kazakhstan, involving inmates who allegedly organized a group defiance and assaulted staff. Ten inmates, mostly young men, face criminal charges. Some inmates claim they self-harmed in protest against alleged mistreatment by prison staff.

item.title: Afghanistan's Heritage Rooted in Wisdom, Not Isolation, Says Ambassador Andisha
item.description: Afghanistan's Ambassador to Switzerland, Nasir Ahmad Andisha, stated that the country's civilizational heritage is based on wisdom, research, and philosophy, not isolation and fear. He emphasized that commemorating figures like Ibn Sina highlights Afghanistan's contributions and the current deprivations faced by Afghan women.

item.title: Kazakhstan Citizens Complain About Difficulties Accessing Healthcare Under Mandatory Insurance
item.description: Kazakh citizens are reporting difficulties accessing doctors and free medical examinations under the mandatory social health insurance system. Issues include inconvenient appointment times for therapists and long waits, up to three months, for ultrasound appointments, while paid services are readily available.
